newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps gain, CFDs by few cents, mogas $3-4.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps gain, CFDs by few cents, mogas $3-4.

text.p: European oil swaps all gained on Monday to varying degrees with Brent CFDs firming by a few cents a barrel and gasoline rising $3-4 a tonne.

The bullish tint to the market was derived from tension between Iraq and the United Nations over the Security Council adopting a resolution over the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.

Brent CFDs also got a boost by a wet deal 41 cents stronger than Friday, but then retraced some of the gains later. This week was pegged around -25 cents against August Brent while June 30-July 4 was valued at about -30 cents. Earlier in the day a CFD traded at -32 cents.
July 7-11 was put at -32 cents from -34 cents and July 14-18 was assessed at -27 cents from -35 cents.

Heavy fuel swaps faced a quiet, albeit slightly firmer day. July hovered around $82.00 to $82.75 for much of the day with August ranged between $83-84. Fourth quarter was bid up later in the afternoon to $91-92.
Gasoline swaps traded a couple of times at $182.00 with physical Eurograde cargoes assessed around $190 cif NWE.
Naphtha tracked up $1 a tonne with July hovering around $174.50 from $173.50 while the contango into August remained steady at about $1.
